detail: picked "Cannot end that policy year merely because the rate went up"

N.J.A.C. 11:4-41.3(b)7iii(2) says that when the rate is redetermined more often than annually, the policy shall not terminate in any policy year solely because of a change in the interest rate during that year. The stem's quarterly reset and rate-increase-alone facts trigger exactly this rule, so no second option is defensible.
No strong form cue. A is the only option that is not a termination or conversion outcome, but the other options are parallel and plausible.
